title: RBAC: add rollout.approve/rollout.abort/rollout.edit permissions + enforce on Dedicated rollout APIs
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description: This PR introduces three new RBAC permissions for Dedicated staged rollouts (rollout.edit, rollout.approve, rollout.abort) and enforces them across the control-plane rollout APIs. Motivation: we currently rely on coarse-grained operator/admin checks, which is too permissive for enterprise Dedicated tenants and makes it hard to reason about approvals vs. editing vs. emergency abort. Scope: add permissions to the authz policy bundle, wire them into the API handlers (create/update/approve/abort), and add tests to prevent regressions. Notes: read-only endpoints (get/list/status) continue to use existing read permissions (rollout.read / dedicated.pool.read) and are unchanged except for a small refactor to reuse the new authz helper. By default, enterprise tenants do NOT get these permissions unless explicitly granted via role mapping (feature-flag allowlist still applies on top of RBAC). Related: approval/abort endpoints in #28462 and audit events in #28558; this PR focuses on who is allowed to call those endpoints, and ensures we fail closed with a clear 403 + audit trail when callers are missing permissions. Rollout behavior: if the authz service is unavailable, we fail closed for mutating actions (edit/approve/abort) and return 503 to callers; this matches our enterprise change-management posture for Dedicated.

control-plane: enforce rollout.approve and rollout.abort on stage actions (0b6d44c)

refactor: centralize rollout authz checks + consistent error mapping (c3e58dd)
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Can we confirm we fail closed for approve/abort if authz is degraded? Also, please make sure we do not leak permission names or internal role IDs in 403 payloads for enterprise tenants.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Yes — mutating actions fail closed. I updated http_mapping.go to return a generic "forbidden" message and moved details into server logs with request_id (no role IDs). Added a unit test for the error mapping.

Chloe Martin (review): Requesting change: please avoid sprinkling RequirePermission(...) calls across handlers. Can we centralize per-action checks in a helper so Console backend gets consistent error codes/messages?

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Done. Added internal/rollouts/authz_helpers.go with RequireRolloutEdit/RequireRolloutApprove/RequireRolloutAbort and updated handlers to use them. Integration tests updated accordingly.
Ethan Park (review): Looks good. One question: do we need rollout.edit for plan "dry-run validate" endpoint? (I know this PR doesn’t add it, but we should decide.)

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Good point. I left validate under read-only for now since it doesn’t persist state, but I added a TODO in the handler and linked it to ENG-5129 comments. Happy to tighten in a follow-up once we align with Product/SRE.
Jordan Lee (review): Please confirm the permission check happens before any side effects (including emitting events).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Confirmed — checks occur at handler entry before touching state or emitting events. Added a regression test asserting no audit event is emitted on 403 for approve/abort.
Felix Schneider (review): Thanks. For Console, we rely on distinct error codes to show "Request approval" vs "Contact admin"; does this still return 403 consistently?
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Yes, 403 for forbidden, 401 for unauthenticated, 503 when authz backend is unavailable. Error codes are stable; Console can key on status + error_code field (unchanged).
Marcus Lin (review): Approved. Please coordinate with Kevin on export pipeline if any new permission strings need to be mapped in audit exports.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Ack — no audit schema change in this PR; permission strings are only internal authz. Will sync with Kevin if we decide to surface permissions in admin UI later.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated staged rollouts now have explicit RBAC permissions for edit/approve/abort, enforced across rollout APIs; enterprise tenants remain default-deny unless explicitly granted.
